analysis.one_liner: TMPV is Tata Motors' car and SUV business, including Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) and a majority stake in Tata Technologies, split off in October 2025 from the commercial-vehicle business that now trades separately as Tata Motors Ltd (TMLCV).
analysis.whats_happening: TMPV's Q2 FY27 results (quarter ended 30 September 2026), released around 13 November 2026, showed consolidated revenue up 34% YoY to about ₹96,920 crore, but a consolidated net loss of roughly ₹5,451 crore after ₹6,738 crore of exceptional items at JLR (employee separation and asset impairment). Before exceptional items, consolidated profit before tax was a thin ₹403 crore. Domestic retail volumes rose 40% to a record 201,723 units and EV volumes rose 90% to 47,150 units, while JLR returned to a small profit, helped mainly by a weak year-ago quarter when a cyberattack halted its production for about six weeks.
analysis.plain_terms: TMPV is what used to be called Tata Motors, minus the trucks and buses business, which now trades as a separate company. Three things are happening inside it at once: Indian car and EV sales are genuinely growing fast, JLR's reported profit swing looks dramatic but is mostly a comparison against a crippled quarter last year (a cyberattack stopped production for weeks), and the company just booked a large accounting loss from one-off restructuring and write-off charges. None of these three threads move in the same direction, so headline revenue growth or a reported loss alone doesn't tell you much - you have to look at each piece separately.
analysis.quarters: Revenue growth has been real and volume-led on the domestic side - retail units up 40% YoY and EVs up 90% YoY in the September 2026 quarter, a record for the India business. Consolidated numbers are dominated by JLR, whose revenue rose 20.3% YoY to £5.89 billion and swung to a marginal profit (£6 million for the quarter, £115 million for the half) against losses a year earlier - but that prior-year period was depressed by a six-week production halt from an August-September 2025 cyberattack, so the YoY comparison overstates the improvement in JLR's underlying run-rate. Underlying EBIT margin was still only 1.1%. The reported consolidated net loss of about ₹5,451 crore is driven almost entirely by ₹6,738 crore of exceptional items (employee separation, asset impairment, restructuring), not by weak operating performance - this looks like a cleanup quarter rather than a demand problem.
analysis.performance_read: The -74.8% drawdown from the July 2024 peak and the negative 3-5 year returns shown for TMPV should not be read as a straightforward crash: in October 2025 the old combined Tata Motors demerged, and every existing shareholder received one TML Commercial Vehicles Ltd (now Tata Motors Ltd, ticker TMLCV) share for each old share, on top of keeping their TMPV share. TMLCV listed around ₹335 in November 2025. A price series that tracks only TMPV misses the value of those distributed TMLCV shares entirely, so the true return to a long-term holder who kept both legs is materially better than the standalone TMPV numbers suggest - though the combined figure cannot be quantified precisely without a verified current TMLCV price. Within that caveat, TMPV has also underperformed Nifty and Maruti over 1 and 3 years even before the split is accounted for, reflecting JLR's troubles (cyberattack, tariffs, China weakness) sitting on top of the demerger effect.
analysis.valuation_read: The reported P/E of roughly 1.3-1.4x looks extremely cheap, but this is very likely an artifact of a large one-off gain sitting in trailing earnings (consistent with demerger accounting and this quarter's exceptional items) rather than a genuine bargain - a stock priced at little more than one year of normal earnings is not plausible for a company of this scale, so this number should not be taken at face value. P/B of about 0.98x, close to book value, is a more believable reference point. ROE and ROCE are cited very differently across sources (ROE anywhere from 18% to 76%, ROCE from 2.7% to 20%) and could not be verified against a filing - treat both as Not verified - check on Screener. Against Maruti Suzuki (P/E ~24.6x, ROE ~13.9%), TMPV's low multiple largely reflects JLR's currency, tariff and cyclical exposure sitting inside a consolidated number that isn't really comparable to a pure domestic ICE/CNG business like Maruti's.
analysis.growth_read: Domestic growth is clearly volume-led - retail units up 40% and EVs up 90% YoY, with Tata now India's second-largest PV maker and holding about 40.7% of the EV share of the PV market. At the consolidated level, though, most of the swing in reported profit comes from JLR's recovery off a cyberattack-depressed base rather than margin expansion - consolidated EBIT margin was still only 1.1%, so this is a recovery story layered on top of real domestic volume growth, not yet evidence of durable margin improvement.
analysis.health_read: Net debt rose sharply across the last two quarters - from about ₹30,700 crore at the end of FY26 to ₹42,200 crore in June 2026 to ₹50,800 crore by September 2026 - even as revenue grew, which is worth watching. The quarter's net loss was driven by one-off exceptional charges rather than weak cash operating performance, so this looks more like business risk (JLR's cyberattack recovery, a potential US tariff hit of up to £1.6 billion before mitigation, soft China demand) than acute financial risk for now; CRISIL and ICRA have both reaffirmed stable AA+ ratings. Whether this quarter's pre-exceptional profit is backed by actual cash generation is Not verified - check on Screener.
analysis.ownership_read: Tata Sons holds about 40% directly, with total promoter holding around 42.5%. FII and DII holding figures varied widely across sources (FII roughly 15-17%, DII anywhere from 7% to 18%) and could not be reconciled to a single reliable number. No evidence of promoter pledging was found, but zero pledging could not be positively confirmed from an official filing either - pledging status is Not verified - check on Screener. No specific marquee individual or institutional investor was identified on the register in this research.
strengths: Domestic retail volumes up 40% YoY to a record 201,723 units in Q2 FY27, with EV volumes up 90% YoY to 47,150 units
Tata now holds about 40.7% share of India's EV passenger-vehicle market and is the country's #2 PV maker by volume
JLR revenue grew 20.3% YoY to £5.89 billion and returned to profit as cyberattack-related disruption faded
Credit ratings reaffirmed stable (CRISIL AA+/A1+, ICRA) despite the loss-making quarter
watchpoints: Net debt nearly doubled from ₹30,700 crore (FY26-end) to ₹50,800 crore (September 2026) in two quarters
JLR faces a potential US tariff hit of up to £1.6 billion (management says mitigated to about £600 million) plus continued weak China demand
Reported P/E (~1.3x) and ROE/ROCE figures vary wildly across sources and look distorted by one-off items - do not take them at face value

The -74.8% price drawdown since July 2024 is inflated by the October 2025 demerger: shareholders also received TML Commercial Vehicles (TMLCV) shares (listed ~₹335) that a TMPV-only price chart does not capture
analysis.one_thing: Whether JLR's EBIT margin (1.1% this quarter) climbs meaningfully from here, or whether this quarter's profit swing was purely a low-base comparison against the 2025 cyberattack - the next 1-2 quarters of JLR margin data will resolve this.
analysis.data_notes: Demerger terms (1:1 TMLCV distribution, effective 1 Oct 2025) and Q2 FY27 headline revenue/loss/volume figures were cross-checked across multiple financial media sources (Business Standard, Autocar Pro, HDFC Sky, Kotak Neo) and corroborate. Could not verify: ROE/ROCE (conflicting figures across sources), promoter pledging status, exact DII shareholding percentage, next results/AGM date, and a current verified TMLCV share price to quantify combined post-demerger shareholder returns - all flagged as Not verified - check on Screener.
